provenance.changes: Declared changes only. (1) imports rewritten from top-level to package-relative; (2) the HuggingFace Hub dependency and PyTorchModelHubMixin base class removed; (3) the input channel count is a constructor argument (cfa4 builds fnet 4 / cnet 8, rgb3 builds fnet 3 / cnet 6) instead of the hard-coded 3/6; (4) ResNetFPN takes an explicit depth argument and its torchvision ImageNet branch is deleted, so model depth and pretrained-weight loading are independent and no configuration can re-enable a download; (5) the 2 * (x / 255) - 1 RGB rescale is removed from RAFT.forward, so callers must supply calibrated, normalised RAW values; (6) in utils/utils.py the scipy import is local to forward_interpolate because scipy is not a dependency of this repository and no vendored model path calls it; (7) ruff format applied (whitespace/docstring layout only). Author definitions are otherwise unchanged: compare executable_ast_sha256 per file.
provenance.ast_digest_rule: executable_ast_sha256 = sha256 of '\n'.join(canonical(node) for each top-level FunctionDef/ClassDef of the module AST after docstring statements are removed), where canonical(node) = (node type name, ((field name, canonical(value)), ...)) over ast.iter_fields, skipping the CPython-version-dependent field 'type_params' (PEP 695, present on FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef/ClassDef from 3.12 on, absent on 3.11). Every other field is always emitted, including empty lists, so CPython 3.13's ast.dump show_empty=False default cannot move a digest either. The digest is identical under CPython 3.11 and 3.12.

known_differences_and_risks: the vendored tree ships no core/loss.py, so sequence_loss is re-implemented with the fetched upstream sha256 recorded in the module docstring; the only declared difference is a mask-sum clamp so an empty mask contributes zero instead of NaN
no upstream pretrained or ImageNet weights are loaded (model.pretrained_checkpoint = null); every seed starts from its seeded random initialisation

the shipped noise-config geometry is 64x64 sensor (32x32 packed), below the vendored 4-level correlation pyramid minimum of 128 packed cells at iters>0; the training config overrides to 256x256 sensor and scales every pixel-valued recipe length by 4 (translation_subpixel tokens stay absolute)
LR drops are declared at absolute updates (50k, 80k); extending a resumed run therefore replays the same LR trajectory instead of moving phase boundaries
checkpoint size is ~226 MB per file (19.7M params + AdamW moments); last.pt is overwritten every 1000 updates and best.pt on every improvement

validation_plateau is a stop condition, not a quality verdict: a run whose validation only degrades also has 'no improvements' for eight checks; the receipt carries the whole validation history and the best checkpoint

the old_simplified arm is a global integer correlation alignment on the delivered RAW planes (the old align_planes path needs a given offset field, so this arm supplies it); its variance shortcut is not reused
the evaluation caps region sizes case-balanced so every case (and every bucket) keeps at least one pair

d1_platform_criteria_fix.defect: D1: decide_platform accepted a constant or monotonically degrading validation curve as validation_plateau
fix: flat_tail_below_delta_val stays literal: slow persistent improvement below delta_val is still a plateau
d1_platform_criteria_fix.operational_note: decide_platform is called only with the validation history; the fix changes neither the training trajectory nor any checkpoint's tensor content. An already-finished run whose old receipt says validation_plateau on a zero-improvement or drifting curve must have its status re-derived (the checkpoint stores val_history/lr_drops, so this is a pure recomputation), and a run that is still executing keeps the old function in memory until restarted; it never needs an update rerun.

policy_preflight.crop_constraint_disclosure: the vendored 4-level correlation pyramid requires >=128 packed cells per side; rgb3 has SENSOR_PER_PACKED=1 so --crop 32 was geometrically impossible. crop=128 gives 128x128 packed, exactly the rgb3 dev arm's training geometry. This is the declared geometry floor, not a relaxation to pass a check.

disclosures: The rgb3 motion model used by the real-platform preflight is a 256-update dev arm (run_scale=dev, budget_exhausted, reasons 'fewer than two validation points (1)'). It demonstrates interface/gradient/single-arrival connectivity only, not alignment quality.
Formal motion-quality evidence is the three-seed CFA evaluation on the synthetic-CFA test split; it is reported separately from the real three-channel preflight.
Whether to train an rgb3 arm at the formal budget (~4 GPU-h at current throughput) is left to the research lead; not started.
Evaluation latency is end-to-end estimate() wall time on one already-arrived pair, excluding data rendering.
